title: Indirect contribution has a vacuous oracle: delete the statement under test and the fixture still prints ok=1
detail: The only CHECK is V(c)-2.0*V(p) == 0.0, and both operands come from the fixture's own `//! bias V(p)=0.75` / `//! bias V(c)=1.5` lines. Verified in src/backend/tb.zig:385-387: bias values are written straight into x[] and the testbench never solves, so the residual is 1.5-1.5=0.0 identically whatever the module body contains. A compiler that dropped `V(p):V(c)==2.0*V(p)` entirely passes. The header's claim that the solver 'moves V(p) until the stated equation holds' is not what the harness does.
expected: Assert something the indirect statement itself determines, not the bias pair. Cheapest honest form: keep only ONE biased node and let the constraint fix the other, or -- if the harness cannot solve -- convert to `//! reject` with a DEBT header saying the suite has no way to exercise 5.6.7 and pin the E-code, so nobody reads it as green coverage. Do not leave a CHECK whose two sides are both `//! bias` inputs.

title: 09_generate.va is a GREEN POSITIVE on a body Annex A cannot derive, and its invariant cannot see an under-unrolled loop
detail: Two defects in one file. (1) A.4.2 `generate_block ::= module_or_generate_item | begin [:id] {module_or_generate_item} end`, and an analog statement is only a module_or_generate_item via `analog_construct ::= analog analog_statement`. This fixture writes `generate for(...) begin `CHECKI(...); I(p,n) <+ ...; end endgenerate` with NO `analog` keyword, which no production derives -- a conforming compiler rejects the file. Verified against the binary: `generate for(i=0;i<2;i=i+1) analog I(p)<+V(p); endgenerate` (the CONFORMING form) is rejected by VerA with E0209 'expected an expression: found analog', while the non-conforming form compiles. So the suite's only loop-generate positive rewards the bug. (2) `index*index-index==0` is zero for index 0 and 1; an unroll that emitted only one copy prints one ok=1 line and nothing counts lines, so under-unroll is invisible.
expected: Replace the invariant with an accumulator whose final value pins the TRIP COUNT, the way ch03_data_types/09_genvar.va already does (`acc = 0+1+2` -> CHECKX 3.0). And either write the conforming `analog` form and pair it with a DEBT header + `//! reject E0209` (VerA cannot parse it), or state in the header that the un-keyworded body is a VerA extension and not Annex-A syntax. Do not leave it reading as a conformance positive.

title: 14_if_generate.va demands a diagnostic for if-generate, which VerA ALREADY SUPPORTS -- it can become a real positive today
detail: Verified against zig-out/bin/vera: `module m(p); ... parameter integer e=1; generate if(e) I(p)<+V(p); else I(p)<+0.0; endgenerate endmodule` lints CLEAN, and so does the named-block form `generate if(e) begin : on I(p)<+V(p); end else begin : off I(p)<+0.0; end endgenerate`. The only reason this fixture errors is the redundant `analog` keyword inside the generate block (E0209 'expected an expression: found analog'), i.e. it errors on the one part of the line that IS conforming. §6.6.2 and A.4.2 define if-generate normatively and Annex C.8 puts all of Clause 6 in the Verilog-A subset (C.16 excludes only the connect/wreal keyword family), so a conforming compiler fails this fixture. Highest value item in the chapter: it converts a bogus reject into real coverage of a construct that works.
expected: Positive fixture. `parameter integer enabled = 1;` + `generate if(enabled) I(p)<+2.0*V(p); else I(p)<+0.0; endgenerate`, biased `//! bias V(p)=0.5`, asserting the TAKEN arm ran and the other did not -- e.g. a real `sel` set in each arm, `CHECKX("the true arm of an if-generate is the one elaborated", sel, 2.0)`. Add `//! lrm A.4.2` + `//! lrm 6.6.2`. Note in the header that the `analog` keyword inside the block is what VerA cannot take (E0209) and file that as the residual gap.

title: 24_expression_composites.va rejects LEGAL concatenation and replication, and says so in its own first line
detail: The file opens 'DEBT -- this rejection is NOT conformance' and then cites §11.6.19, a VPI object-model clause, as the rule for source-level semantics. §4.2.13 defines concatenation and replication normatively and Annex C.5 excludes exactly one thing from Clause 4 in Verilog-A -- the case equality operators === and !== -- so `{4'b1010,4'b0101}` and `{2{4'b0011}}` are legal. Verified: VerA fails at E0207 'unexpected token: found {' on the replication. Sibling evidence that the gap is partial, not principled: ch03_data_types/28_string_replication.va uses `{3{"ab"}}` as a GREEN POSITIVE. So the suite both requires and forbids replication.
expected: Split. Keep a reject that pins the real VerA gap with the stable code (`//! reject E0207`) under a DEBT header citing §4.2.13 and A.8.1 -- not §11.6.19 -- and stating plainly that a conforming compiler accepts this. Move the parts VerA DOES support (`~`, `<<`, `&`, `?:` on integers) into a separate positive with digits, so the operator coverage this file claims is not lost behind the concatenation failure.

title: 15_case_generate.va demands a ParseError for case-generate, which §6.6.2 requires a compiler to accept
detail: Verified: VerA emits E0205 'unsupported module item: found case' -- a genuine VerA gap, unlike A03 this one cannot be turned into a positive today. But the fixture states the gap as if it were the rule: bare `//! reject ParseError`, no cite, and a trailing 'normative syntax/restriction snapshot for this rule family' comment that reads as conformance. Annex C.8 puts Clause 6 in the Verilog-A subset; C.16 does not exclude generate.
expected: Keep the reject, pin the stable code `//! reject E0205` instead of the phase label, add `//! lrm A.4.2` + `//! lrm 6.6.2`, and put the DEBT header on it (the same wording ch04_expressions/31_replication_rejected.va uses) so the file records a VerA limitation, not a language rule. Drop the 'normative snapshot' trailer.

title: 13_parameter_port_list.va demands a ParseError for the legal ANSI `#(...)` module parameter port list
detail: A.1.3 `module_parameter_port_list ::= # ( parameter_declaration { , parameter_declaration } )` and A.1.2 admits it in module_declaration; nothing in Annex C removes it. Verified: VerA emits E0207 'unexpected token: found #  expected `;`', and src/frontend/parser.zig:198 says so outright -- 'ponytail: no module_parameter_port_list (#(...), A.1.3). The header expects `;` after the port list, so `#` reports "expected semicolon" -- which is what the fixtures pin.' The fixture pins the bare label `ParseError` while a stable code exists.
expected: Keep the reject, switch to `//! reject E0207`, add `//! lrm A.1.3` + `//! lrm 6.2`, add the DEBT header. If `#(...)` is ever implemented, this becomes the positive: `#(parameter real gain=2.0)` with `//! param gain = 3.5` and `CHECKX("header parameter takes its override", gain, 3.5)`.

title: 10_paramset_rejected.va demands E0201 for a legal paramset -- and E0201's own title concedes it
detail: §6.4 defines paramset normatively; Annex C.8 puts all of Clause 6 in the Verilog-A subset and C.16's exclusion list does not name it. E0201's title in src/diag_code.zig is literally 'construct is not in the supported subset' -- a statement about VerA, pinned as if it were a statement about the language. No `//! lrm`, no DEBT header.
expected: Keep the reject (the gap is real), add `//! lrm A.1.9` + `//! lrm 6.4` and the DEBT header stating a conforming compiler accepts this file. One edit, no new digits.

title: 11_module_instantiation_rejected.va demands E0204 for a legal module instantiation
detail: §6.2.2 defines module instantiation and A.4.1 gives the grammar; C.8 keeps Clause 6 in Verilog-A. E0204's help text ('compile the child as its own device and instantiate it in the netlist', parser.zig ~line 410) is a workflow decision for VerA, not a rule of the standard. COVERAGE.md restates the inversion as policy: 'hierarchy is rejected rather than flattened incorrectly'.
expected: Keep the reject, add `//! lrm A.4.1` + `//! lrm 6.2.2` and the DEBT header. Note in it that annex_e_spice/*.va already instantiate BUILT-IN primitives by name (`inductor #(.l(1n)) x(.p(p),.n(n));`), so the refusal is specific to user modules.

title: 12_defparam_rejected.va demands E0205 for a legal defparam, and its body would not be a valid positive either
detail: §6.3.1 defines the defparam statement and A.1.4 `parameter_override ::= defparam list_of_defparam_assignments ;` is a module_or_generate_item. C.8 keeps it in Verilog-A. Separately, the module body is `defparam child.gain = 2.0;` with no instance named `child` anywhere in the file, so even a compiler that implemented defparam would have to reject it -- for a different reason than the one the fixture claims.
expected: Keep the reject, add `//! lrm A.1.4` + `//! lrm 6.3.1` and the DEBT header; and give the file a real instance to override so the hierarchical name resolves, otherwise the fixture is pinned to two independent errors and will keep passing after the first is fixed.

title: 17_named_event_trigger.va is green for the wrong reason: the diagnostic fires on the LEGAL `event tick;`, never on the illegal `-> tick;`
detail: Verified against the binary: the only diagnostic is E0203 'named event declaration is not implemented' pointing at column 55, the `event` keyword. A.2.1.3 makes `event tick;` legal and ch05_analog_behavior/named_event_unsupported.va argues at length in its own header that named events ARE in the Verilog-A subset (5.10.4's example lives inside an analog block; C.7 excludes DIGITAL events). The two things in this line that Annex A actually forbids -- `-> tick;` in analog_statement position (A.6.4 lists event_trigger only under analog_event_statement) and `@(tick) I(p)<+V(p);` (no contribution_statement alternative in analog_event_statement) -- are never reached. The assertion is the bare label `DiagnosticsReported`, which any error satisfies.
expected: Split into two files. (a) Keep this one as the named-event DEBT reject with `//! reject E0203` + `//! lrm A.2.1.3` + `//! lrm 5.10.4`, saying VerA has not implemented a legal construct. (b) The A.6.4 event_trigger prohibition needs a fixture that reaches it, which is impossible while `event` is refused -- record that dependency in the header rather than pretending it is tested. Also fold in the uncovered lens's `@ hierarchical_event_identifier` (no-parens) form: it too requires a named event and is blocked behind the same E0203, so it needs no separate fixture.

title: 20_task_enable.va never reaches the illegal construct: E0205 fires on the `task` DECLARATION, not on the call
detail: Verified: `error[E0205]: unsupported module item: found task` at column 55 -- the declaration. A.2.7 makes a task_declaration a module item, and the thing A.6.4 forbids is the ENABLE (`record(V(p));` in analog_statement position; analog_statement has no task_enable alternative). The fixture asserts only `ParseError`, so it would stay green if VerA started accepting task declarations and then silently accepted the call too.
expected: Point the fixture at the call. If task declarations must stay refused, say so in the header and pin `//! reject E0205`; then add the A.6.4 claim as a separate note stating it cannot be reached yet. Add `//! lrm A.6.9` + `//! lrm A.6.4`.

title: 22_port_branch_rejected.va pins VerA's parse failure on the LEGAL port branch, with no cite and a message-substring assertion
detail:
A.2.1.3 `port_branch_declaration ::= branch ( < port_identifier > ) list_of_branch_identifiers ;` and §3.12.1 Port Branches make `branch (

) port_path;` legal. Verified: VerA emits E0208 'expected an identifier: found <'. The fixture asserts the substring `identifier`, which is prose, not a code -- and note that src/diag_code.zig carries a purpose-built E0304 'port branches are not supported' that NO fixture references and that this syntax never reaches. Nothing in the suite demands the port branch work.
expected: Rewrite with `//! reject E0208` + `//! lrm A.2.1.3` + `//! lrm 3.12.1` + the DEBT header. Separately worth a bug: E0304 is dead code, the parser errors first.

title: nature_attribute_unsupported.va pins `expected )` on the legal A.8.9 nature_attribute_reference, and admits it in its own comment
detail: A.8.9 `nature_attribute_reference ::= net_identifier . potential_or_flow . nature_attribute_identifier` is a legal analog primary, and §5.5.3 Accessing attributes gives its value. The fixture's own EXPECT line says 'net.potential.abstol is not represented by the AST' -- a statement about VerA -- while the assertion is the raw parser message `expected `)``. No lrm cite, no DEBT header, so it reads as if the standard forbade the form.
expected: Rewrite with the stable code, `//! lrm A.8.9` + `//! lrm 5.5.3`, and the DEBT header. The value to demand when it is implemented is the bound nature's abstol: for `electrical` that is Annex D's 1e-6, so `CHECKX("p.potential.abstol is the bound nature's abstol", p.potential.abstol, 1e-6)`.

title: Three ch04 fixtures RUN analog-function forms 4.7.1 forbids, each admitting it in its own header
detail: A.10 detail 1 is 'Function statements are limited by the rules of 4.7.1', and 4.7.1 requires a function to 'have at least one formal argument declared' and that 'all formal arguments shall have an associated block item declaration specifying the data type', and 'shall not use named blocks'. Verified the three headers say so themselves: 100_function_no_arguments.va ('a strict reading rejects this module rather than running it. VerA accepts it'), 101_function_untyped_argument.va ('strictly a violation and a conforming tool may reject this module'), 99_function_named_block_ban.va ('a conforming tool diagnoses this file. VerA has no diagnostic for the rule today'). All three are green positives, so a compiler with the same three holes passes.
expected: This is exactly what `//! xfail` was built for (README: 'the LRM says the construct is an error, the fixture demands the diagnostic, and VerA does not produce it yet'). Convert each to `//! reject <code>` + `//! lrm 4.7.1` + `//! xfail VerA accepts <form>, 4.7.1 forbids it`. Three files, one convention. Note the suite currently contains ZERO `//! xfail` and ZERO `//! lrm` lines across all 859 fixtures, so these are the first users of both directives.

title: want 5.0 is only right on the FIRST evaluation of the analog block; a conforming iterating simulator gets 7.0
detail: `case (index)` reads an integer that is never assigned before it. §3.2: integers are initialized 'at the start of a simulation'. §5.6.1.3: 'Unlike variables, the contributed value for a branch is only valid for the current iteration' -- i.e. variables DO retain across iterations. §5.2: 'Analog blocks shall be executed at every point in a simulation.' So from the second execution on, `index` holds the 3 the `while` left, the case takes `default:` (+3 not +1), and the trace is 0 -> 1 -> 4 -> 5 (for) -> 7 (repeat) = 7.0. Recomputed and confirmed. It passes only because tb.zig evaluates once from a fresh State. The `//! bias`-independent CHECKI on index (3) is fine.
expected: Make the case arm depend on something the fixture sets: `index = 0;` before the `case`, keeping want 5.0 and the same derivation; or keep the uninitialised read and move it into its own fixture that asserts the §3.2 zero-initialisation directly. Fix the header at the same time -- it cites '§3.3.1' for the initialisation rule and there is no §3.3.1 (3.3 is String data type; the rule is §3.2).

title: `active == 1` from above() in a standalone DC point is permitted by 5.10.3.2, not required by it
detail: Read the clause end to end: the two `shall` sentences are scoped. 'If the expression is positive at the conclusion of the initial condition analysis THAT PRECEDES A TRANSIENT ANALYSIS, the above() function shall generate an event' and 'During a DC SWEEP, the above() function shall also generate an event when the expression crosses zero from below'. What covers this fixture is only the permissive 'the cross() function will not generate events for non-transient analyses ... but the above() function CAN'. The fixture runs a plain DC operating point with no sweep and no transient, and demands the event.
expected: Either move it under a directive that triggers a `shall` -- `//! time 0, 1n` (IC preceding a transient) or a `//! sweep` that crosses zero from below -- and keep want 1; or keep the DC point and weaken the claim to the part that IS normative in DC: cross() must NOT fire. The second is one line and loses nothing, since the fixture's stated purpose is the cross/above contrast.

title: A rule VerA already enforces (E0406, contribution inside an event statement) has ZERO fixtures
detail: A.6.4 `analog_event_statement` lists no contribution_statement alternative, and §5.10 says 'Contribution statements cannot be used inside an event control block because it can generate discontinuity in analog signals'. Verified two ways: `grep -rl E0406 tests/fixtures` returns nothing, and the binary emits exactly `error[E0406]: contribution inside an event statement` for `analog begin @(cross(V(p),1)) I(p)<+V(p); I(p)<+0.0; end`. The two files that contain the construct today (annex_a_syntax/17, ch05/named_event_unsupported.va) both die on the named-event E0203 first -- ch05's header even says so: 'This rule IS enforced (see lower.zig) ... it is simply not the first diagnostic here.' Delete the check in lower.zig and the whole suite stays green.
expected: //! lrm A.6.4 + //! lrm 5.10 + //! reject E0406. Body: `analog begin @(cross(V(p), 1)) I(p) <+ V(p); I(p) <+ 0.0; end` -- cross(), not a named event, so E0203 is never reached.

title: E0411 (indirect contribution inside an event statement) is enforced and referenced by no fixture
detail: Same shape as C01 for the indirect form: A.6.4 analog_event_statement has no indirect_contribution_statement alternative. Verified: zero fixtures grep for E0411; the binary emits `error[E0411]: indirect contribution inside an event statement` for `analog begin @(cross(V(p),1)) V(p):V(c)==2.0*V(p); I(c)<+0.0; end`. Needs its own file because a reject fixture stops at the first diagnostic.
expected: //! lrm A.6.4 + //! reject E0411, with the cross()-guarded indirect contribution above.

title: E0703 (nested event control statement) is enforced and referenced by no fixture
detail: A.6.4 `analog_event_control_statement ::= analog_event_control analog_event_statement` and analog_event_statement has no analog_event_control_statement alternative, so `@(a) @(b) stmt;` is underivable. Verified: zero fixtures grep E0703; the binary emits `error[E0703]: nested event control statement` for `analog begin @(initial_step) @(cross(V(p),1)) x=1.0; ... end`.
expected: //! lrm A.6.4 + //! reject E0703, body as above.

title: E0408 (contribution target must be a branch access) is enforced and referenced by no fixture
detail: A.6.10 `contribution_statement ::= branch_lvalue <+ analog_expression ;` -- the left side must be a branch access, never a variable. Verified: zero fixtures grep E0408, and no fixture in the suite writes a contribution whose lvalue is not V(...) or I(...). The binary emits `error[E0408]: contribution target must be a branch access` for `real x; analog begin x <+ 1.0; ... end`.
expected: //! lrm A.6.10 + //! reject E0408. Body: `real x; analog begin x <+ 1.0; I(p) <+ V(p); end`.

title: force/release/assign/deassign are never tested in analog_statement position -- the three existing fixtures die on `reg`/`initial` first
detail: A.6.2 procedural_continuous_assignment is an alternative of the DIGITAL `statement` only; no production puts it inside `analog`. Verified the three ch08_scheduling fixtures (procedural_force_unsupported.va, procedural_release_unsupported.va, procedural_deassign_unsupported.va) all wrap the construct in `reg` + digital `initial`, so they are rejected for E0205/`reg`/`initial` and prove nothing about the analog position. The binary emits E0209 'expected an expression: found force' for `analog begin force x = 1.0; ... end`. A compiler that accepted force inside analog passes the suite today.
expected: //! lrm A.6.4 + //! lrm A.6.2 + //! reject E0209, body `real x; analog begin force x = 1.0; I(p) <+ V(p); end`. Sibling files for release/assign/deassign are optional -- they take the same parser path and the same code; add them only if that path ever diverges.

title: No fixture puts a nonblocking assignment inside an analog block
detail: A.6.4 analog_procedural_assignment derives only the blocking `=` form; `<=` is digital. Verified: no `.va` in the suite has a statement-level `<=` (every hit is a relational operator in an expression), and ch08_scheduling/nonblocking_unsupported.va uses `always @(source) target <= source;` so it dies on the digital process. The binary emits `error[E0214]: expected '<+' or '=': found `;`` for `analog begin x <= 1.0; ... end` -- note the diagnostic reads as a typo for `<+`, which is exactly the confusion worth pinning.
expected: //! lrm A.6.4 + //! reject E0214, body `real x; analog begin x <= 1.0; I(p) <+ x*V(p); end`.

title: fork/join, wait, and delay control are never tested in analog_statement position
detail: A.6.3 par_block (`fork ... join`), A.6.5 wait_statement and A.6.5 delay_control are all alternatives of the digital `statement`; analog_statement derives none of them. Verified suite-wide: the only `fork`/`wait`/`deassign` occurrence is annex_b_keywords/10_task_control_keywords.va, which puts them inside a `task` and so never reaches an analog context, and the only `#N` is ch08_scheduling/blocking_timing_unsupported.va inside `reg`+`initial`. The binary emits E0209 for all three in analog position ('found fork', 'found wait', 'found `#`').
expected: Three small files, same shape: 31_fork_in_analog_rejected.va, 32_wait_in_analog_rejected.va, 33_delay_control_in_analog_rejected.va, each `//! lrm A.6.4` + the owning production + `//! reject E0209`. They cannot share one file: a reject fixture stops at the first diagnostic.

title: A.10 detail 4, second sentence -- 'A system_function_identifier or system_task_identifier shall not be escaped' -- is untested suite-wide
detail: Verified: `grep -rn '\\\$'` over all 859 fixtures returns nothing. The FIRST sentence of the same note ('The $ character ... shall not be followed by white_space') is covered by ch02_lexical/18_system_whitespace_rejected.va (`$ vt`), which is why both the uncovered and negatives lenses landed on the same gap from opposite sides. The binary does reject `x = \$vt;` -- the lexer takes `\$vt;` as one escaped identifier terminated by the space and then E0207s on the next token -- so the negative is writable today.
expected: //! lrm A.10 + //! lrm 2.8.3 + //! reject E0207, body `real x; analog begin x = \$vt ; I(p) <+ x*V(p); end`. Say in the header WHY it fails (the backslash makes it an ordinary identifier, not the system function), because the diagnostic alone does not.

title: A.10 detail 2 'Embedded spaces are illegal' is tested for based numbers only, never for real_number
detail: ch02_lexical/36_based_number_digit_whitespace.va covers `8'h Af`; nothing covers a real. The hazard is a lexer that glues `1.5 e3` into 1500.0. Verified: VerA rejects it with E0207 'unexpected token: found e3', so the fixture is green today.
expected: //! lrm A.10 + //! lrm 2.6.2 + //! reject E0207, body `real x; analog begin x = 1.5 e3; I(p) <+ x*V(p); end`.

title: 01_source_text.va asserts NOTHING, and the nature/discipline it declares are dead text
detail: The file declares `nature annex_a_voltage` and `discipline annex_a_electrical` and then binds its nets with the BUILT-IN `electrical`, so a compiler could discard both declarations and still pass. There is no CHECK and no `//! reject`, so torture reports it unasserted and it fails only under --strict. It is the nominal fixture for A.1.2 `description ::= module_declaration | nature_declaration | discipline_declaration` and proves none of the three.
expected: Bind the nets to the DECLARED discipline and assert through it: `//! bias V(p)=0.6` + `//! bias V(n)=0.1` + `annex_a_electrical p, n;` + `CHECK("the user-declared nature's access function reaches the node pair", V(p,n), 0.5, 1e-15)` (0.6-0.1 = 0.5 exactly in binary; verified). Same edit gives A.1.3 `list_of_port_declarations ::= ()` a home for free: change the port-less `module annex_a_first;` to `module annex_a_first();` -- verified to lint clean. That module stays CANNOT RUN (zero terminals, per README), which is the correct verdict, not a pass.

title: `analog function` with the TYPE OMITTED (defaults to real) appears in no fixture -- an integer-defaulting compiler passes today
detail: A.2.6 makes analog_function_type optional and §4.7.1 is explicit: 'The analog_function_type specifies the return value of the function; its use is optional. type can be real, integer, or string; if unspecified, the default is real.' Verified: every one of the suite's analog functions writes `real`; `grep -rnE 'analog +function +[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]* *;'` returns zero hits. A compiler that defaulted to integer would truncate and still pass the whole suite. Verified runnable: I built and ran `analog function sq; input real x; sq = x*x; endfunction` at V(p)=1.5 and VerA returns 2.25 -- so this fixture is green on day one and pins the rule.
expected: //! lrm A.2.6 + //! lrm 4.7.1 + //! bias V(p) = 1.5, then `CHECK("an analog function with no declared type returns real", sq(V(p,n)), 2.25, 1e-15)`. 2.25 is exact in binary; an integer default returns 2.0 and fails by 0.25.

title: `analog function integer` and `analog function string` appear in no fixture
detail: A.2.6 `analog_function_type ::= integer | real | string`. Verified: zero hits suite-wide for either. Verified both lint clean and the integer form runs -- `analog function integer sgn; input real x; sgn = (x>0.0) ? 3 : -3; endfunction` returned 3 at V(p)=1.5 under the built testbench.
expected: One file, two functions. `CHECKI("an integer-typed analog function returns an integer", sgn(V(p,n)), 3)` and, for the string form, the comparison shape ch03_data_types/25_string_nul_removal.va already uses: `CHECKI("a string-typed analog function returns its assigned string", (name(1.0) == "hi"), 1)`. //! lrm A.2.6 + //! lrm 4.7.1.

title: Branch ARRAYS (`branch (p,n) b[0:1];` + `V(b[0])`) appear nowhere in the suite, and VerA cannot parse them
detail: A.2.3 `list_of_branch_identifiers ::= branch_identifier [ range ] ...` and A.8.9 `branch_reference ::= hierarchical_branch_identifier [ constant_expression ]`. Verified: zero hits across 859 files; every branch declared anywhere is scalar. Verified against the binary: `branch (p,n) pair[0:1];` fails with E0207 'unexpected token: found `[` expected `;`' -- so this must be a DEBT reject, not a positive. Note src/diag_code.zig carries E0305 'branch arrays are not supported' which NO fixture references and which this syntax never reaches (the parser errors first) -- worth a separate bug.
expected: //! lrm A.2.3 + //! lrm A.8.9 + //! reject E0207 + DEBT header. Record the value it must produce when implemented: with `//! bias V(p)=0.8` / `//! bias V(n)=0.3`, both `V(pair[0])` and `V(pair[1])` name the same node pair, so both are 0.5 (0.8-0.3 is exact in binary; verified).

title: `-inf` as a value_range bound appears nowhere -- only the `inf` upper half is covered
detail: A.2.5 `value_range_expression ::= constant_expression | -inf | inf`. Verified: the only `-inf` hits in the suite are prose about floor() rounding; 44 files use `inf)` as an upper bound and none uses the lower. Verified `parameter real g = 1.0 from (-inf:inf);` lints clean, so this needs no new file.
expected: One-line edit to 03_declarations.va, which already carries `parameter real gain = 2.0 from (0:inf)`: add `parameter real bipolar = -0.5 from (-inf:0];` and `CHECKX("a parameter bounded below by -inf keeps its negative default", bipolar, -0.5)`. -0.5 is exact. Add //! lrm A.2.5.

title: `analog_case_item ::= default [ : ]` -- the OPTIONAL colon after `default` -- is never exercised
detail: A.6.7 makes the colon optional. Verified: every `default` in a case body across the suite is written `default:`. Verified `case (m) 0: r=1.0; default r=2.0; endcase` lints clean in VerA, so the coverage is free.
expected: Fold into 05_behavioral_statements.va, which already has a case statement, when B01 rewrites it: drop the colon on its `default` arm and say in the header that A.6.7 makes it optional. Zero new files, and it makes the B01 rewrite pay for itself.

title: `abstol_expression ::= constant_expression | nature_identifier` -- a filter tolerance that NAMES a nature -- is never used
detail: A.8.3 lets an analog operator's tolerance argument be a nature identifier rather than a number. Verified: 72 filter/operator calls in the suite pass tolerances and every one is numeric. Verified `analog I(p) <+ ddt(V(p), Voltage);` lints clean in VerA, so a positive is writable.
expected: //! lrm A.8.3, one operator call with the nature name as its tolerance argument, plus an assertion the tolerance does not change (e.g. the ddt of a DC bias is 0.0 at the first time point, `CHECK(..., 0.0, 1e-15)`), so the file proves the form PARSES and BINDS rather than silently dropping the argument. Cross-check the nature name against the Annex D prelude the compiler prepends.

title:
23_expression_primaries.va's header claims the port probe `I(

detail:
The header lists 'a port probe I(

) (A.8.2 port_probe_function_call)' among the primaries the file covers. In the body `I(

title: `port ::= . port_identifier ( [ port_expression ] )` -- a named port in the module HEADER -- appears nowhere
detail: Verified: every `.name(x)` hit in the suite is an INSTANTIATION-side named connection in annex_e_spice; no module header uses the A.1.3 named-port form, where the external name differs from the internal net. Verified `module np(.ext(inner), n); ...` fails with E0208 'expected an identifier: found `.`', so this is a DEBT reject, not a positive.

title: `port_expression ::= { port_reference { , port_reference } }` -- a concatenated port -- appears nowhere
detail: Verified: no module header in the suite contains a brace-concatenated port. Verified `module cp({a,b}, n); ...` fails with E0208 'expected an identifier: found `{`'.

title: `module_keyword ::= macromodule` with an ANALOG body is untested; the one macromodule fixture is digital and pinned to a VerA refusal
detail: A.1.2 makes macromodule interchangeable with module, and nothing in Annex C removes it (C.16 excludes only the connect/wreal keyword family). The only fixture is annex_b_keywords/11_macromodule_keyword.va, which is `macromodule annex_b_macro(input a, output b); assign b=a; endmodule` -- digital, and pinned `//! reject NoModule`, so it proves nothing about the analog case and reads as if macromodule itself were out of the subset.

title: A.6.9 makes the analog_system_task_enable argument list optional AND individual arguments empty; neither shape is tested
detail: A.6.9 `analog_system_task_enable ::= analog_system_task_identifier [ ( [ analog_expression ] { , [ analog_expression ] } ) ] ;`. Verified both `$strobe;` (no parens) and `$strobe("a",,"b")` (empty middle argument) are accepted by VerA -- only W0850 'display task dropped' is emitted in device mode.

Weakest item in the tier -- do it only in a pass that is already touching the chapter.

title: Nine header citations name the wrong clause, and they are about to be transcribed verbatim into `//! lrm` directives
detail: Checked every one against docs/VAMS-LRM/*.html section headings: 05 and 16 cite '3.3.1' for the initialisation rule and §3.3.1 DOES NOT EXIST (3.3 is String data type; the rule is §3.2). 02 cites '3.5' for ANSI ports -- 3.5 is Genvars; ports are §6.5. 03 cites '3.7' for branches (3.7 is Real net declarations; branches are §3.12) and '3.4.5' for aliasparam (3.4.5 is Local parameters; parameter aliases are §3.4.7). 07 cites '4.1.5' for the precedence table and '4.1.13' for the conditional operator -- neither exists; they are §4.2.2 and §4.2.12. 08 cites '2.7' for escaped identifiers -- 2.7 is String literals; escaped identifiers are §2.8.1. 23 cites '3.9' for a real array word select -- 3.9 is Disciplines of primitives; real arrays are declared in §3.2. 19 cites '5.9' for 'The return statement can only be used from within an analog user-defined function' -- I read that sentence in §5.11 Jump statements; 5.9 is Looping statements, and sibling 18_disable_statement.va gets it right and even documents the earlier mis-cite. All the NUMERIC wants in these headers recompute correctly; only the clause numbers are wrong. Also folded in here: 02's prose says the probe is 'exactly 0.5 V' when 0.7-0.2 = 0.49999999999999994 (the CHECK's 1e-15 tolerance is correct; only the word 'exactly' is wrong -- 23's header gets the same arithmetic right and says so).
expected: Eight file header edits, no assertion changes. Do this BEFORE the `//! lrm` rollout (E02), not after -- a wrong cite in a directive is worse than a wrong cite in a comment because --coverage will index it. Two of the .expected-error.txt sidecars duplicate the wrong §5.9 text and go away with E04.

title: Not one fixture in the chapter carries a `//! lrm` directive -- including the two rejects that are correct
detail: Verified suite-wide, not just here: `grep -rl '^//! lrm'` over all 859 fixtures returns ZERO, as does `grep -rl xfail`. Both directives are fully documented in tests/fixtures/README.md and implemented in tests/torture.zig (parsed, printed on failure, indexed by --coverage), and nothing uses them. Until they exist, `--coverage` prints an empty table and the claim 'Annex A is covered' has no mechanical backing.
expected: 24 one-line additions, using the corrected numbers from E01. 18_disable_statement.va is the model: it already reasons about which clause owns the rule and why. Six rejects should switch from bare phase labels to stable codes at the same time (13 -> E0207, 15 -> E0205, 17 -> E0203, 20 -> E0205, 14 -> whatever survives A03, 24 -> E0207) -- README: 'Codes are the preferred form'.

title: COVERAGE.md documents VerA's failure classes as if they were the chapter's dispositions
detail: Its closing sentence states the policy outright: 'Where VerA rejects a normative form, the precise current failure class is paired instead of claiming generated support.' The table then books seven anti-conformant rejects as coverage -- 'A.1 paramset: 10_paramset_rejected.va verifies deliberate loud rejection', 'A.4 module instantiation: hierarchy is rejected rather than flattened incorrectly', and 13/14/15/24 under 'Production completion ... no longer disposition-only'. Read as a coverage claim for the STANDARD, every one of those rows is inverted.
expected: Rewrite the affected rows once A01-A09 land: split the table into 'covered by a positive', 'covered by a conforming negative', and 'VerA gap on a legal production (DEBT)'. The third column is the honest home for paramset, defparam, instantiation, #(...), case-generate, concatenation, branch arrays, port branches and named ports -- and it is the number the chapter should be judged on.

title: Eleven `.expected-error.txt` sidecars survive here against the README's 'No sidecar files'
detail: README.md line 3: '859 .va files. One runner, tests/torture.zig. No sidecar files.' and 'there is no second file to drift out of step with it'. The chapter has 11 (10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24), several holding only the bytes 'error' or a phase label already stated in the .va, and two duplicating header prose including the wrong §5.9 cite E01 fixes. Note the scope: there are 301 of these suite-wide, so this chapter's 11 are one slice of a global cleanup -- confirm the runner truly ignores them before deleting (I found no reference to 'expected-error' anywhere in torture.zig).
expected: Delete the 11 files. Nothing to add: every one of them restates something the .va already says.
